page.layout: One page of text in verse and headings; notes in the right margin. Running head at top centre; page number at top right.

main_text.p: Tot Galata, tot Pontus eat, tot Lydia nummis. Idem in Eo-tro.lib.2.
Si Lyciam tenuisse velis, tot millia ponas

p.i: Quid tamen expectant, Phrygio quos tempus erat iam Galli Phry-gum sacer-dotes.
More superuacuam cultris abscindere carnem. Iuuen.Sat.2.
Num tu, qua tenuit Dives Achemenes? Horat. carm. lib.2.
Aut pinguis Phrygia Mygdonias opes, Mygdonia & Achemenia dicta Phry-gia.
Permutare velis crine Licinia? Ouid.Trist. lib.1.

main_text.head: Dardania, eadem est quae & Phrygia.

p.i: Dardaniamque petit auctoris nomen habentem:
Et te ruricola Lampsace tuta deo.
Quaque per angustas male vexta virginis undas Virg.Georg. lib.1.
Sestion Abydena separat urbe fretum.

main_text.head: Abydus urbs Phrygiae.

p.i: —ostriferi fauces tentantur Abydi.

main_text.head: Troas regio Phrygiae à Troia urbe Phrygiae appellata.

p.i: Caesar ut Emathia satiatus clade recessit, Luc.lib.12.
Caetera curarum proiecit pondera, soli
Intentus genero: cuius vestigia frustra
Terris sparsa legens, fama duce tendit in undas,
Threiciaque legit fauces, & amore notatum Hellespon-tus. Sestus. Abydus.
Aequor, & Eoas lacrymoso litore turres,
Qua pelago nomen Nepheleias abstulit Helle.
Non Asiam breuioris aquae disterminat vsquam
Fluctus ab Europa, quamuis Bizantion arcto Bizantion oppidum. Chalcedo oppidum.
Pontus, & ostriferam dirimat Chalcedona cursu,
Euxinumque ferens paruo ruat ore Propontis.

page.notes: Marginal notes on the right are set in small type and were transcribed as printed. Some notes are abbreviated and their line placement is approximate. Some words in the body, including "Dives" and "Abydi", were read with some uncertainty.
